newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Lippo says minimum fee scheme beneficial.
newsitem.headline: Lippo says minimum fee scheme beneficial.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Lippo Securities said on Thursday it saw a proposed stock market regulation, which reportedly includes introducing minimum brokerage transaction fees, as benefiting the industry.
"The minimum fee will benefit us and others," president director Charles de Queljoe told Reuters.
A Jakarta stock exchange official said the current regulation only limits the maximum brokerage transaction fee to one percent but did not limit the minimum fee.
The official declined to give details on the proposed regulation, adding it is now being reviewed by the capital market supervisory agency (Bapepam).
De Queljoe said some brokerage firms were even willing to charge transaction fees below 0.25 percent which he regarded as unprofitable and which could lead to unhealthy competition.
He said some firms charged between 0.85 and one percent in transaction fees for clients, usually institutions, which demanded full services such as research and continued updates.
Brokerage firms generally charge retail investors around 0.65 percent, he said.
